zeta at index 1 of the known pair.

tail-resumptive UZero convention at the artifact so M4's abandon cut is
a measured flip, never an accident. The measurements: abort()'s arm
value (None) returns to the PERFORM site and does not unwind —
`abort(); 0` discards it, so the try/catch protocol sees Some(0) and
the catch never runs (M4 flips this program 0 to 42, documented in the

exhaustive else (measured first-hand: the naive crucible shape trapped
exactly there). The 33 pin survives the abandon cut; only the
fragility disappears.

convention erases the observable (the arm value returns to the perform
site regardless of which handler record dispatched), so the A2
arbitration gate lands with the abandon cut, where install-value
delivery makes the resolution visible. The resolution mechanism itself
— the no-config singleton tier reading $<hname>_state_g live under the
resume-site bracket — is already the dispatch in place.

mentl/a3ab460:
Root cause: emit_make_variant stored the variant pointer in $__vptr, then
evaluated field expressions. Nested allocations (empty lists, inner variants,
tuples) inside field expressions clobbered $__vptr via local.tee. The final
local.get $__vptr returned the wrong pointer — variant tags read as 0 or 4
instead of the correct tag_id (14 for FnStmt).

Fix: evaluate ALL field expressions first into __f0..__f5 temp locals, THEN
allocate the variant and store tag + fields. No nested allocation can clobber
$__vptr because allocation happens AFTER all field evaluation is complete.

Verified: parsed FnStmt tag = 14, direct FnStmt tag = 14. Tags match.
8/8 crucibles pass (wasm_check needs separate fix for apply() map lambda).

clob/a351a41:
The crystallization loop previously did not close end-to-end:
  - Episodes recorded a hardcoded actual_token=0 → prediction_error was noise
  - CrystallizationEngine::apply_modules had zero callers
    → crystallized modules never affected inference
  - distill ignored actual_token and used avg(h - centroid) which cancels to ≈0
    → rank-1 weights had near-zero magnitude even when modules did fire
  - Multiple crystal cycles overwrote module_00000000..7.mod → no accumulation
  - Ingest silently clamped tokens > vocab_size to vocab-1
    → half of BPE vocab collapsed to one token with no warning

Changes:
- cmd_ingest streams tokens via decode_step; records real (context, actual, p_actual)
  per step. Prediction error = 1 - P(actual). State carries across the whole corpus.
- CoreModel owns Vec<CrystalModule> and applies them in decode_step between
  final_norm and unembed, routed by cosine similarity > activation_threshold.
  Additive, scaled by similarity.
- distill::distill takes &[f32] embedding table; correction direction is
  avg(embed[actual_i] - h_i) weighted by prediction_error — gradient-aligned
  under tied unembed. Falls back to hidden-centroid when no embedding is given.
- CrystalModule and TernaryMatrix gain Serialize/Deserialize; new crystal::store
  handles save_module / load_modules for .mod files on disk.
- cmd_crystal / cmd_crystal_with_model run one cycle and save new modules.
  next_module_id scans the directory so cycles accumulate instead of overwriting.
- cmd_eval scores a corpus token-by-token and prints mean NLL + perplexity.
  Emits a single JSON line on stdout for scripting.
- assert_vocab_compatible hard-fails on tokenizer.vocab > model.vocab.
  Deleted the silent clamp in cmd_ingest and cmd_think.
- cmd_boot stops writing garbage episodes (hardcoded actual_token=0); its
  :crystal REPL passes the embedding table and saves modules to disk.
- KernelConfig::small (d=128, L=4, V=1024) — fits a 512-merge BPE tokenizer
  without vocab mismatch

stoop/a377e5c:
Somebody handed an issue file used to get its text and nothing else: the
stencil headline came out as a line of typewriter, the stamps were gone,
and the photographs lost where they were glued. The file now opens on the
pages as made, cover alone and then the spreads, scaled to the screen and
stacked a page at a time on a phone, with the text one tap away for a
screen reader or a slow connection. The shelf reads back issues the same
way. One page renderer serves the file, the shelf and the printed sheet.

A cutting run over the gutter between facing pages shows on both, on
screen, in the file, in the browser's print and in the PDF, each page
drawing its neighbour's overhang as though the two were one sheet, which
on the one-sheet fold they are. It is stored once, where it was placed.

Back issues ride in a file with their covers' photographs only. Each has
its own file with the rest, and carrying every photograph on the shelf
made a file grow with every issue. A photograph a file does not carry
shows as an empty place that says where it lives. A new cutting now takes
the keyboard from whatever page field was focused, so the arrows move it.
stoop/a349a08:
An exported issue used to open on the shelf, inside the app's header and
seven tabs, with the issue itself one click further in. Somebody who
scanned the back of a zine was holding paper a moment ago; what they get
now is the issue and nothing else, and at the end of it the press they are
already holding offers itself: make the next number, start your own, or
see the shelf. The file's own hint about where to open still travels, but
the reader decides that paper comes first, so every issue exported before
this change lands the same way. Starting your own clears the issue you
were handed, so the first file you pass on carries only your own work and
not somebody else's first number in its archive.

The sheet accepts what lands on it. A photograph dragged in from the
desktop is dithered and glued down where it fell; text dragged or pasted
in becomes a cutting there, a short line as a headline and a paragraph as
typewriter copy. The tray and its arm-then-click remain for now, but they
are no longer the way a thing gets onto the paper. A drop on a panel that
prints upside down lands where the pointer was, because the drop point
goes through the same panel-local measurement the drag gestures use.

A photograph glued to the paste-up was not a live reference: the sweep
would have collected it as an orphan and the export left it out of the
file, so the cutting travelled and its picture did not. Both walk the
paste-up now, and the suite checks that a glued-down photograph is in the
seed on the machine that opens the file.

The press is 182 KB built, ten under the ratchet. That is the ratchet
doing its job: the next moves take the nav, the tray and most of the view
chrome out, and the number comes back down.
